statements.text: American technological leadership is vital to our economic and national security. Shipping advanced chips to our primary competitor is a sure way to lose that lead. The American people want AI innovation that creates good jobs at home, not that advances our adversaries' efforts to modernize their militaries and hollow out our industry. With this legislation, Congress is sending a clear message that there is bipartisan support for protecting our competitive edge to the benefit of all Americans.
statements.venue: Statement on AI OVERWATCH Act introduction

statements.text: Partnership with the UK and Australia on advanced capabilities, such as AI, cyber, and quantum technologies, will further U.S. leadership on emerging technology by enhancing our joint capabilities, interoperability, and fostering deeper information and technology sharing with our closest allies.
statements.context: Written responses to Senate Foreign Relations Committee questions for the record during the nomination hearing for a U.S. Ambassador to the UK.

statements.text: I appreciate NIST's efforts on mitigating AI bias and the development of the Risk Management Framework. What activities has NIST planned to provide actionable guidance to reduce the risks from AI bias? [...] NIST contributes to the research, standards, and data necessary to advance characteristics of trustworthy artificial intelligence, including mitigation of harmful bias, in order to realize the full promise of this technology. [...] Managing bias is also included as one of the key trustworthiness characteristics outlined in the NIST AI Risk Management Framework which NIST is developing hand-in-hand with the larger community. This Framework will provide guidance to organizations on how to manage risks of AI systems.
statements.context: Written Q&A exchange during Senate Appropriations Subcommittee hearings for Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies FY2023, with Senator Schatz questioning Commerce Secretary Raimondo.

statements.text: Well, I will just close with this. I agree with the concerns that have been raised by other Committee Members and you with TikTok. To me, TikTok is a Chinese AI weapon aimed directly at the United States of America, and we better take it seriously, so, among other things. Thank you, [...]
statements.context: Senator Shaheen delivers closing remarks during a Senate Armed Services Committee hearing on the FY 2024 Defense Department authorization request.

statements.text: We also need to harness artificial intelligence and innovation to make sure that we're maximizing the utility of new capabilities.
statements.context: Senate Appropriations Subcommittee hearing on DHS's Fiscal Year 2024 budget, during an exchange on fentanyl interdiction at ports of entry.

statements.text: How does the Department look at how we ensure that those inequities are not part of whatever is done through AI, particularly with respect to gender or with respect to the whole range of ethnic racial differences that we want to respect?
statements.context: Senator Shaheen poses a question during a hearing on U.S. AI leadership in strategic competition.

statements.text: The discussions that took place just recently on the AI, you may not be aware, but every senator is going through AI 101, 102, 103, and 104—I think the last classes are this week—and we are looking at how we can get a handle on AI from a regulatory—from a government regulatory point of view.
statements.context: Senate hearing on transnational repression; the senator pivots from disinformation by adversaries to senators' AI education classes and upcoming AI legislation.

statements.text: I am convinced the proliferation of disinformation and misinformation about our elections and political system pose one of the gravest threats facing the United States today. I am concerned that future uses of deepfake technology will be harder to detect and fend off as AI technology progresses. The federal government should use all the authority at its disposal to find and punish those using AI and related technology to break the law.
statements.venue: Letter to DOJ and CISA on AI deepfake robocalls (press release)

statements.text: As the federal government works to address the risks posed by rapidly developing AI technologies, preserving the integrity of the election process and protecting the fundamental right to vote is paramount.
statements.venue: Letter to DOJ and CISA on AI deepfake robocalls (press release)

statements.text: During the New Hampshire primary back in January we had a domestic actor who used artificial intelligence to voice clone President Biden's voice and to target voters on a roboscam in New Hampshire.
statements.context: Senate Intelligence Committee Worldwide Threats hearing, with Senator Shaheen questioning the Director of National Intelligence on AI-enabled election interference.

statements.text: Russia, in particular, has engaged in the use of artificial intelligence, generative AI in the context of their information operations.
statements.context: Senate Intelligence Committee hearing on worldwide threats, with Director of National Intelligence Haines responding to Senator Shaheen's question.

statements.text: And this bill actually tries to prohibit States from regulating AI for the next 10 years, making it that much harder to keep our kids safe online and to protect jobs from being lost to the use of this technology.
statements.context: Senator Shaheen delivers floor remarks opposing a budget reconciliation bill that includes a moratorium on state AI regulation.

statements.text: How are we responding? I mean, this was a domestic issue, but it points to the potential challenges from AI, and the threat that that can present to our elections. [...] And how are we sharing—how is the FBI sharing what you know with local law enforcement and election officials so that everybody is aware of what the threat is?
statements.context: Senate Appropriations subcommittee hearing on CJS appropriations, with Senator Shaheen questioning FBI Director Wray about AI-enabled disinformation and election security.

statements.text: Question 7. Madam Secretary, the Department in its FY 2025 request is asking for $62.1 million in new funding related to artificial intelligence (AI). This includes new funding for BIS, NTIA, and NIST. As I mentioned at the hearing, given the FRA caps, I suspect we may be in a similar position as FY 2024 where we have to make difficult decisions to meet our allocations.
statements.context: Written questions for the record from a Senate appropriations hearing on Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies funding for FY2025.

statements.text: AI, to create sexually explicit photos and videos that appear to be real, it complicates investigations because it is difficult to tell what is real and what is not.
statements.context: Senate Appropriations Subcommittee hearing on the FY2025 Commerce, Justice, Science budget, with Senator Shaheen questioning FBI Director Christopher Wray.

statements.text: Other countries have recognized the importance of investing in S&T and are now challenging U.S. preeminence in several critical technologies such as microelectronics and semiconductors, advanced communication, artificial intelligence, and high-performance computing. Ensuring our nation's prosperity now and in the future demands robust investment in S&E research, education, and infrastructure, with a renewed focus on translating scientific discoveries as well as innovations into new or improved products and processes in across America.
statements.context: Written NSF response to Senate Appropriations subcommittee questions for the record on FY2025 CJS appropriations.

statements.text: In this budget, I am asking for $60 million in NIST for AI. Honestly, that is a drop in the bucket for all of the testing, evaluation, and safety work that we have to do for artificial intelligence.
statements.context: Senate Appropriations subcommittee hearing on the Commerce Department's FY2025 budget, where Secretary Raimondo defends NIST funding requests for AI and quantum work.

statements.text: AI holds extraordinary potential for both promise and peril. Harnessing AI for good requires mitigating its risks.
statements.context: Secretary of Commerce Gina Raimondo's prepared testimony before the Senate Commerce-Justice-Science Appropriations Subcommittee on the FY2025 budget request.

statements.text: funding for NIST to establish an Artificial Intelligence Safety Institute, and funding for NTIA to better serve States and territories in administering the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law Broadband programs.
statements.context: Senate appropriations hearing on the Department of Commerce's FY2025 budget request, with Senator Shaheen chairing and Secretary Raimondo testifying.

statements.text: The H200s are vastly more capable than anything China can make and gifting them to Beijing would squander America’s primary advantage in the AI race.
statements.venue: Joint statement by Shaheen, Coons and other Democratic senators on Nvidia H200 exports to China

statements.text: I hope that Congress can do a better job of addressing the technology around AI than we've done to address the other technology companies that have been responsible for social media and some of the excesses of social media. But sadly, right now, there is very little that is moving forward in Congress to address it.
statements.venue: WMUR 'Conversation with the Community' town hall

statements.text: One of the things that there is real bipartisan concern about is allowing the advanced chips to go to China
statements.venue: Brookings Institution event (reported by Export Compliance Daily)

statements.text: I think it's important for Congress to weigh in on this, because it says to the administration: this is something that we're watching. We're paying attention to this on a bipartisan basis, and you should not do it

statements.text: In the 21st century, economic and national security is increasingly defined by a nation’s ability to adopt and deploy cyber and related technologies [...] This legislation sends a message to the world: the United States will compete on technology, and we can offer a better deal.
statements.venue: Statement on U.S. Tech PATH Act with Sen. Ricketts (MeriTalk)
